# 7-Zip

7-Zip is a file archiver with a high compression ratio.

## About

7-Zip is free software that provides:
- High compression ratio using the LZMA and LZMA2 compression algorithms
- Support for multiple archive formats (7z, ZIP, GZIP, BZIP2, TAR, and others)
- Strong AES-256 encryption in 7z and ZIP formats
- Self-extracting capability for 7z format
- Integration with Windows Shell
- Powerful command-line interface
- Plugin support for file managers

## Website

Official website: [7-zip.org](https://7-zip.org)

## License

7-Zip is distributed under the GNU LGPL license (with some components under other open-source licenses).
See the DOC directory for detailed license information.

## Supported Formats

**Packing / unpacking**: 7z, XZ, BZIP2, GZIP, TAR, ZIP and WIM

**Unpacking only**: APFS, AR, ARJ, CAB, CHM, CPIO, CramFS, DMG, EXT, FAT, GPT, HFS, IHEX, ISO, LZH, LZMA, MBR, MSI, NSIS, NTFS, QCOW2, RAR, RPM, SquashFS, UDF, UEFI, VDI, VHD, VHDX, VMDK, XAR and Z.

For more information, visit the official 7-Zip website.

7-Zip is a file archiver for Windows.

License Info
------------

7-Zip is free software distributed under the GNU LGPL
(except for unRar code). Also some  code
is licensed under the "BSD 3-clause License".
Read "License.txt" for more infomation about license.

Notes about unRAR license:

Please check main restriction from unRar license:

   2. The unRAR sources may be used in any software to handle RAR
      archives without limitations free of charge, but cannot be used
      to re-create the RAR compression algorithm, which is proprietary.
      Distribution of modified unRAR sources in separate form or as a
      part of other software is permitted, provided that it is clearly
      stated in the documentation and source comments that the code may
      not be used to develop a RAR (WinRAR) compatible archiver.

In brief it means:
1) You can compile and use compiled files under GNU LGPL rules, since
   unRAR license almost has no restrictions for compiled files.
   You can link these compiled files to LGPL programs.
2) You can fix bugs in source code and use compiled fixed version.
3) You can not use unRAR sources to re-create the RAR compression algorithm.


LZMA SDK
--------

This package also contains some files from LZMA SDK
You can download LZMA SDK from:
  http://www.7-zip.org/sdk.html
LZMA SDK is written and placed in the public domain by Igor Pavlov.


How to compile in Windows
-------------------------

To compile the sources to Windows binaries you need Visual Studio compiler and/or Windows SDK.
You can use latest Windows Studio 2017/2019/2022 to compile binaries for x86, x64, arm64 and arm platforms.
Also you can use old compilers for some platforms:
  x86   : Visual C++ 6.0 with Platform SDK
  x64   : Windows Server 2003 R2 Platform SDK
  ia64 (itanium)  : Windows Server 2003 R2 Platform SDK
  arm for Windows CE : Standard SDK for Windows CE 5.0

If you use MSVC6, specify also Platform SDK directories at top of directories lists:
Tools / Options / Directories
  - Include files
  - Library files

Also you need Microsoft Macro Assembler:
  - ml.exe for x86
  - ml64.exe for x64
You can use ml.exe from Windows SDK for Windows Vista or some later versions.

There are two ways to compile 7-Zip binaries:
1) via makefile in command line.
2) via dsp file in Visual Studio.

The dsp file compiling can be used for development and debug purposes.
All final 7-Zip binaries are compiled via makefiles, that provide best
optimization options.


How to compile with makefile in Windows
---------------------------------------

Some macronames can be defined for compiling with makefile:

PLATFORM
  with possible values: x64, x86, arm64, arm, ia64

OLD_COMPILER
  for old VC compiler, like MSCV 6.0.

MY_DYNAMIC_LINK
  for dynamic linking to the run-time library (msvcrt.dll).
  The default makefile option is static linking to the run-time library.

To compile all 7-Zip files for x64 with Visual Studio 2022,
use the following command sequence:

  cd SRC\CPP\7zip
  %comspec% /k "C:\Program Files\VS2022\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat"
  nmake

You can use another "vcvars*.bat" files from "VS2022\VC\Auxiliary\Build" directory
to compile for other platforms:
  vcvars64.bat
  vcvarsamd64_arm64.bat
  vcvarsamd64_x86.bat

Also you can compile single binary from directory with related project.
For example, to compile 7za.exe, use the following command sequence:
  cd SRC\CPP\7zip\Bundles\Alone\
  nmake


Compiling 7-Zip for Unix/Linux
------------------------------

There are several options to compile 7-Zip with different compilers: gcc and clang.
Also 7-Zip code contains two versions for some parts of code: in C and in Assembeler.
So if you compile the version with Assembeler code, you will get faster 7-Zip binary.

7-Zip's assembler code uses the following syntax for different platforms:

1) x86 and x86-64 (AMD64): MASM syntax.
   Now there are 3 programs that supports MASM syntax in Linux.
'    'Asmc Macro Assembler, JWasm, and UASM. Note that JWasm now doesn't support some
      cpu instructions used in 7-Zip.
   So you must install Asmc Macro Assembler in Linux or UASM, if you want to compile
   fastest version of 7-Zip  x86 and x86-64:
     https://github.com/nidud/asmc
     https://github.com/Terraspace/UASM


2) arm64: GNU assembler for ARM64 with preprocessor.
   That systax is supported by GCC and CLANG for ARM64.

There are different binaries that can be compiled from 7-Zip source.
There are 2 main files in folder for compiling:
  makefile        - that can be used for compiling Windows version of 7-Zip with nmake command
  makefile.gcc    - that can be used for compiling Linux/macOS versions of 7-Zip or Windows version
                    with MINGW (GCC) with make command.
                   
At first you must change the current folder to folder that contains `makefile.gcc`:

  cd CPP/7zip/Bundles/Alone2

import struct, zlib, sys
def read_num(d,i):
    b=d[i]; i+=1
    if b<0x80: return b,i
    cnt=0; mask=0x80
    while b & mask: cnt+=1; mask>>=1
    if cnt>=8:
        return int.from_bytes(d[i:i+8],'little'), i+8
    high=b & (0xFF >> (cnt+1))
    low=int.from_bytes(d[i:i+cnt],'little'); i+=cnt
    return (high << (8*cnt))|low, i

class Folder:
    pass

def parse_streams(d,i, verbose=True):
    packpos=None; pack_sizes=[]; folders=[]
    # assume start at id
    while True:
        pid=d[i]; i+=1
        if pid==0:
            break
        elif pid==6: # PackInfo
            packpos,i=read_num(d,i)
            numstreams,i=read_num(d,i)
            print(' PackInfo packpos',packpos,'num',numstreams)
            while True:
                sid=d[i]; i+=1
                if sid==0: break
                elif sid==9:
                    pack_sizes=[]
                    for _ in range(numstreams):
                        v,i=read_num(d,i); pack_sizes.append(v)
                    print('  pack sizes',pack_sizes)
                elif sid==10:
                    alldef=d[i]; i+=1
                    crcs=[]
                    if alldef:
                        for _ in range(numstreams):
                            crcs.append(struct.unpack('<I',d[i:i+4])[0]); i+=4
                    else:
                        raise Exception('pack crc bitset not impl')
                    print('  pack crcs', [hex(c) for c in crcs])
                else: raise Exception(f'packinfo id {sid} at {i}')
        elif pid==7: # UnpackInfo
            print(' UnpackInfo')
            assert d[i]==0x0B; i+=1
            numfolders,i=read_num(d,i)
            external=d[i]; i+=1
            print('  folders',numfolders,'ext',external)
            if external: raise Exception('ext folders')
            for fi in range(numfolders):
                f=Folder(); f.coders=[]
                numcoders,i=read_num(d,i)
                total_in=0; total_out=0
                for ci in range(numcoders):
                    desc=d[i]; i+=1
                    idsize=desc&0xF; iscomplex=bool(desc&0x10); hasattrs=bool(desc&0x20)
                    cid=d[i:i+idsize]; i+=idsize
                    nin=nout=1
                    if iscomplex:
                        nin,i=read_num(d,i); nout,i=read_num(d,i)
                    props=None
                    if hasattrs:
                        psz,i=read_num(d,i); props=d[i:i+psz]; i+=psz
                    f.coders.append((cid,nin,nout,props))
                    total_in+=nin; total_out+=nout
                    print('   coder',cid.hex(),nin,nout, props.hex() if props else None)
                f.total_in=total_in; f.total_out=total_out
                # bind pairs
                numbind=total_out-1
                f.bind=[]
                for _ in range(numbind):
                    a,i=read_num(d,i); b,i=read_num(d,i); f.bind.append((a,b))
                numpacked=total_in-numbind
                f.packed_idx=[]
                if numpacked!=1:
                    for _ in range(numpacked):
                        v,i=read_num(d,i); f.packed_idx.append(v)
                else:
                    f.packed_idx=[0]  # approx find unbound?
                folders.append(f)
            # coders unpack size
            assert d[i]==0x0C, (i,d[i]); i+=1
            for f in folders:
                f.unpack_sizes=[]
                for _ in range(f.total_out):
                    v,i=read_num(d,i); f.unpack_sizes.append(v)
                print('   unpack sizes',f.unpack_sizes)
            if d[i]==0x0A:
                i+=1; alldef=d[i]; i+=1
                print('  folder crc alldef',alldef)
                if alldef:
                    for f in folders: f.crc=struct.unpack('<I',d[i:i+4])[0]; i+=4
                else: raise Exception('folder crc bitset')
            assert d[i]==0, (i,d[i]); i+=1
            print('  end unpack')
        elif pid==8: # SubStreamsInfo
            print(' SubStreamsInfo')
            sub_counts=None; sub_sizes=[]; sub_crcs=[]
            while True:
                sid=d[i]; i+=1
                if sid==0: break
                elif sid==0x0D:
                    sub_counts=[]
                    for f in folders: v,i=read_num(d,i); sub_counts.append(v)
                    print('  numunpack per folder',sub_counts)
                elif sid==9:
                    if sub_counts is None: sub_counts=[1]*len(folders)
                    sub_sizes=[]
                    for fi,f in enumerate(folders):
                        cnt=sub_counts[fi]
                        szs=[]
                        for _ in range(cnt-1): v,i=read_num(d,i); szs.append(v)
                        sub_sizes.append(szs)
                    print('  sub sizes',sub_sizes)
                elif sid==0x0A:
                    # first byte?
                    mode=d[i]; i+=1
                    print('  sub crc mode byte',mode, 'next bytes', d[i:i+16].hex())
                    # Need interpret: if mode ==0? bitset? If 1 all defined?
                    # Let's assume: if ??? 
                    # In spec: BYTE AllAreDefined; if 0 then bitvector
                    total_sub=sum(sub_counts) if sub_counts else len(folders)
                    if mode:
                        for _ in range(total_sub):
                            print('   crc', d[i:i+4].hex()); i+=4
                    else:
                        # bitset (total_sub bits)
                        nbytes=(total_sub+7)//8
                        bits=d[i:i+nbytes]; i+=nbytes
                        print('   crc bitset',bits.hex())
                        for idx in range(total_sub):
                            # bit check order?
                            byte=bits[idx//8]
                            # guess msb first
                            if byte & (0x80>>(idx%8)):
                                print('   crc bit',idx, d[i:i+4].hex()); i+=4

            # store
            for idx,f in enumerate(folders):
                f.sub_count=sub_counts[idx] if sub_counts else 1
                f.sub_sizes=sub_sizes[idx] if sub_sizes else []
        else:
            raise Exception(f'streams id {pid} at {i-1}')
    return {'packpos':packpos,'pack_sizes':pack_sizes,'folders':folders}, i

def bits_list(data_bytes, n):
    # 7z bitvector: first item is most significant bit of first byte (? test)
    out=[]
    for idx in range(n):
        byte=data_bytes[idx//8]
        out.append(bool(byte & (0x80 >> (idx%8))))
    return out

def parse_files(d,i):
    numfiles,i=read_num(d,i)
    print('FilesInfo num',numfiles)
    props={}
    while True:
        pid=d[i]; i+=1
        if pid==0: break
        size,i=read_num(d,i)
        start=i

            ext=d[i]; i+=1

                names=[]
                for _ in range(numfiles):

                    # need align to even boundary for terminator: find utf16 null

                    j=i
                    while d[j:j+2]!=b'\x00\x00': j+=2
                    names.append(d[i:j].decode('utf-16le')); i=j+2
                props['names']=names
                print('  names',names)
            else: print('  external names')
        elif pid in (0x0E,0x0F,0x10):
            nbytes=size
            bits=bits_list(d[i:i+nbytes], numfiles if pid==0x0E else 999)

            props[pid]=d[i:i+size]
            i+=size
        elif pid==0x14 or pid==0x12 or pid==0x13:
            j=i
            alldef=d[j]; j+=1
            defined=[True]*numfiles
            if not alldef:
                nbytes=(numfiles+7)//8; defined=bits_list(d[j:j+nbytes],numfiles); j+=nbytes
            ext=d[j]; j+=1
            times=[]
            for idx in range(numfiles):
                if defined[idx]:
                    times.append(struct.unpack('<Q',d[j:j+8])[0]); j+=8
                else: times.append(None)

        elif pid==0x15:
            j=i; alldef=d[j]; j+=1
            defined=[True]*numfiles
            if not alldef:
                nbytes=(numfiles+7)//8; defined=bits_list(d[j:j+nbytes],numfiles); j+=nbytes
            ext=d[j]; j+=1
            attrs=[]
            for idx in range(numfiles):
                if defined[idx]: attrs.append(struct.unpack('<I',d[j:j+4])[0]); j+=4
                else: attrs.append(None)
            props[pid]=attrs; print('  attrs',[hex(a) if a else a for a in attrs])
            i=start+size
        elif pid==0x0A:
            j=i; alldef=d[j]; j+=1
            print('  crc prop alldef',alldef, d[j:j+32].hex())
            i=start+size
        else:
            i+=size
    return props,i

def parse(path):
    d=open(path,'rb').read()
    assert d[:6]==b'7z\xbc\xaf\x27\x1c'
    off,size,crc=struct.unpack('<QQI', d[12:32])
    print(path, 'len',len(d),'nexthdr off',off,'size',size)
    hdr=d[32+off:32+off+size]
    print('hdr hex',hdr.hex())
    i=0
    if hdr[0]==0x17:
        print(' EncodedHeader')
        info,i=parse_streams(hdr,1)
        # decode header stream
        # packed data at 32+packpos
        # implement later
        return
    elif hdr[0]==0x01:
        i=1
        if hdr[i]==4:
            info,i=parse_streams(hdr,i+1)
            print(' streams info', info)
        if i < len(hdr) and hdr[i]==5:
            props,i=parse_files(hdr,i+1)
        print(' end pos',i,'len hdr',len(hdr))
    else:
        print('unknown hdr first', hdr[0])

for p in sys.argv[1:]: parse(p)

def format_datetime(dt, fractional=False):

def human_size(size):

        unit = 1024*1024; unit_name = "MiB"
    elif size < 10*1024*1024*1024*1024:

    def __init__(self, name, is_dir=False):
        self.name = name  # normalized, '/' separator, no trailing slash
        self.is_dir = is_dir
        self.size = 0 if is_dir else None
        self.packed_size = None
        self.mtime_ns = None
        self.mtime_ft = None
        self.atime_ft = None
        self.ctime_ft = None
        self.win_attr = None  # full 32-bit for 7z or low for zip
        self.mode = None  # unix mode
        self.crc = None
        self.method = ""
        self.encrypted = False
        self.block = None
        self.data = None  # bytes if loaded / to write
        self.source_path = None
        self.is_symlink = False
        self.comment = ""
        self.host_os = None
        self.version = None
        self.offset = None
        self.characteristics = None
        self.folder_flag = None
        self.slt_extra = []  # list of (key,value) extra lines if format specific
        self.archive_type = None
        self.scan_size = None
        self.anti = False
        self.hard_link_to = None
    def clone(self):
        e=Entry(self.name,self.is_dir)
        e.__dict__.update(self.__dict__)
        return e
    def mtime_datetime(self):
        if self.mtime_ft is not None and self.mtime_ft!=0:
            return ft_to_datetime(self.mtime_ft)
        if self.mtime_ns is not None:
            try: return datetime.fromtimestamp(self.mtime_ns/1e9)
            except Exception: return None
        return None
    def get_ft(self):
        if self.mtime_ft is not None: return self.mtime_ft
        if self.mtime_ns is not None: return ns_to_filetime(self.mtime_ns)
        return None
    def compute_crc(self):
        if self.data is not None:
            self.crc = zlib.crc32(self.data) & 0xffffffff
        return self.crc

class Archive:
    def __init__(self):
        self.type = None
        self.entries = []
        self.physical_size = 0
        self.headers_size = None
        self.methods = []  # list of method strings
        self.solid = None
        self.blocks = None
        self.warnings = []
        self.errors = []
        self.props = {}  # key->value lines for header in order list of (k,v) maybe
        self.header_extra_lines = []  # strings
        self.path_display = ""
        self.volumes = 1
        self.total_physical = None
        self.is_split_wrapper = False
        self.inner_name = None
        self.encrypted_headers = False
    def total_size(self):
        return sum(e.size or 0 for e in self.entries)
    def total_packed(self):
        return sum(e.packed_size or 0 for e in self.entries)

# mode helpers
def mode_string(mode, is_dir=False):
    if mode is None:
        # synthesize
        if is_dir: return "drwxr-xr-x"
        return "-rw-r--r--"
    ft = stat.S_IFMT(mode)
    if stat.S_ISDIR(mode): c='d'
    elif stat.S_ISLNK(mode): c='l'
    elif stat.S_ISREG(mode): c='-'
    elif stat.S_ISFIFO(mode): c='p'
    elif stat.S_ISSOCK(mode): c='s'
    elif stat.S_ISCHR(mode): c='c'
    elif stat.S_ISBLK(mode): c='b'
    else: c='?'
    chars=[c]
    for who in [(0o400,0o200,0o100, stat.S_ISUID, 's'), (0o040,0o020,0o010, stat.S_ISGID, 's'), (0o004,0o002,0o001, stat.S_ISVTX, 't')]:
        r,w,x,special,schar = who
        chars.append('r' if mode&r else '-')
        chars.append('w' if mode&w else '-')
        if mode & special:
            chars.append(schar if mode&x else schar.upper())
        else:
            chars.append('x' if mode&x else '-')
    return ''.join(chars)

def win_attr_plain(entry, show_archive=True):
    # 5 chars D R H S A
    w = entry.win_attr
    if w is None:
        return 'D....' if entry.is_dir else '.....'
    low = w & 0xFFFF
    s=''
    s += 'D' if (low & 0x10 or entry.is_dir) else '.'
    s += 'R' if low & 0x01 else '.'
    s += 'H' if low & 0x02 else '.'
    s += 'S' if low & 0x04 else '.'
    s += 'A' if (low & 0x20 and show_archive) else '.'
    return s

def win_attr_letters(entry, show_archive=True):
    w=entry.win_attr
    if w is None:
        return 'D' if entry.is_dir else ''
    low=w & 0xFFFF
    s=''
    if low & 0x10 or entry.is_dir: s+='D'
    if low & 0x01: s+='R'
    if low & 0x02: s+='H'
    if low & 0x04: s+='S'
    if low & 0x20 and show_archive: s+='A'
    return s

# Wildcard matching
def has_wildcard(s, opts=None):
    if opts is not None and opts.spd:
        return False
    return '*' in s or '?' in s

def wildcard_match_component(pattern, name, case_sensitive=True):
    if not case_sensitive:
        pattern=pattern.lower(); name=name.lower()
    # convert to regex
    regex='^'
    for ch in pattern:
        if ch=='*': regex+='.*'
        elif ch=='?': regex+='.'
        else: regex+=re.escape(ch)
    regex+='$'
    return re.match(regex, name, re.DOTALL) is not None

def wildcard_match_path(pattern, path, case_sensitive=True):
    # pattern and path use '/'
    if '/' not in pattern:
        name=path.split('/')[-1]
        return wildcard_match_component(pattern, name, case_sensitive)
    pparts=pattern.split('/'); nparts=path.split('/')
    if len(pparts)!=len(nparts):
        return False
    return all(wildcard_match_component(pp,nn,case_sensitive) for pp,nn in zip(pparts,nparts))

def match_with_dir_pattern(pattern, path, case_sensitive=True):
    # Pattern matching used for archive selection/deletion/extraction:
    # - exact/wildcard full match
    # - if pattern matches a directory name (prefix), all under it match (for non-wildcard dir pattern or wildcard matching dir)
    # returns (selected, is_dir_match?) Caller handles
    if wildcard_match_path(pattern, path, case_sensitive):
        return True
    # pattern without wildcard and path under pattern/
    if '*' not in pattern and '?' not in pattern:
        pat=pattern.rstrip('/')
        if path==pat or path.startswith(pat+'/'):
            return True
    # wildcard pattern could match a leading directory: e.g. pattern 'adir' checked above; pattern '*'? Already full match only component wise; '*' vs 'adir/x.txt' len mismatch so not.
    # If pattern matches a prefix directory of path (for patterns like 'a*' matching dir)
    parts=path.split('/'); pparts=pattern.split('/')
    if len(pparts)<len(parts):
        prefix='/'.join(parts[:len(pparts)])
        if wildcard_match_path(pattern, prefix, case_sensitive):
            return True
    return False

# ---------- scanning disk ----------
class ScanWarning:
    def __init__(self, name, msg):
        self.name=name; self.msg=msg

def errno_msg(e):
    if isinstance(e, OSError):
        return f"errno={e.errno} : {e.strerror}"
    return str(e)

class Scanner:
    def __init__(self, opts, archive_path=None):
        self.opts=opts
        self.archive_path = os.path.abspath(archive_path) if archive_path else None
        self.warnings=[]
        self.items=[]
        self._seen_arc = {}  # arcname -> pattern index for dedup internal
        self.duplicates=[]
        self.inode_map={}
    def _is_archive_file(self, fs_path):
        if self.archive_path is None: return False
        try:
            return os.path.abspath(fs_path)==self.archive_path
        except Exception:
            return False
    def _excluded(self, arcname, fs_path=None):
        # exclude patterns -x
        for (recurse, pattern, is_list) in self.opts.exclude_patterns:
            pats=[]
            if is_list:
                pats=read_listfile(pattern, self.opts)
            else:
                pats=[pattern]
            for p in pats:
                # -x patterns: if pattern has no slash, match basename? 7z exclude matches path pattern?
                # Use match_with_dir_pattern with pattern normalized
                p_norm=p.replace('\\','/')
                if match_with_dir_pattern(p_norm, arcname, self.opts.case_sensitive):
                    return True
                # Also if p matches fs relative path?
        return False
    def _make_item_from_stat(self, fs_path, arcname, st, follow_stat=None, is_symlink_store=False, link_target=None):
        opts=self.opts
        is_dir = stat.S_ISDIR((follow_stat or st).st_mode) if not is_symlink_store else False
        use_st = follow_stat if follow_stat is not None else st
        e=Entry(arcname, is_dir=is_dir)
        e.source_path=fs_path
        if is_symlink_store:
            e.is_symlink=True
            e.mode=st.st_mode
            e.data=link_target.encode('utf-8','surrogateescape')
            e.size=len(e.data)
            e.scan_size=0
            e.mtime_ns=st.st_mtime_ns
            e.mtime_ft=ns_to_filetime(st.st_mtime_ns)
        elif is_dir:
            e.mode=use_st.st_mode
            e.size=0; e.packed_size=0; e.scan_size=0
            e.mtime_ns=use_st.st_mtime_ns; e.mtime_ft=ns_to_filetime(use_st.st_mtime_ns)
        else:
            # regular file or other
            e.mode=use_st.st_mode
            e.size=use_st.st_size; e.scan_size=use_st.st_size
            e.mtime_ns=use_st.st_mtime_ns; e.mtime_ft=ns_to_filetime(use_st.st_mtime_ns)
        # win attr
        mode_val=e.mode if e.mode is not None else (0o40755 if is_dir else 0o100644)
        low=0x8000
        if is_dir: low|=0x10
        else:
            low|=0x20
            if mode_val & 0o222 ==0:
                low|=0x01
        e.win_attr=((mode_val & 0xFFFF)<<16)|low
        # hard link handling
        if opts.snh and not is_dir and not is_symlink_store and use_st.st_nlink>1:
            key=(use_st.st_dev, use_st.st_ino)
            if key in self.inode_map and self.inode_map[key]!=arcname:
                e.hard_link_to=self.inode_map[key]
                e.data=e.hard_link_to.encode()
                e.size=len(e.data)
            else:
                self.inode_map[key]=arcname
        return e
    def _add_item(self, item, pattern_index, internal=False):
        if item.name in self._seen_arc:
            if not internal:
                # explicit duplicate across patterns or explicit repeat
                self.duplicates.append(item.name)
                # still add? Original Add errors; for other commands items are duplicated. Scanner caller decides.
                self.items.append(item); return
            else:
                return
        # archive file exclusion
        if item.source_path and self._is_archive_file(item.source_path):
            return
        if self._excluded(item.name, item.source_path):
            return
        self._seen_arc[item.name]=pattern_index
        self.items.append(item)
    def _add_file_path(self, fs_path, arcname, pattern_index, internal=False):
        opts=self.opts
        try:
            lst=os.lstat(fs_path)
        except OSError as ex:
            self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(arcname if arcname else fs_path, errno_msg(ex))); return
        if stat.S_ISLNK(lst.st_mode):
            if opts.snl:
                try: target=os.readlink(fs_path)
                except OSError as ex:
                    self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(arcname, errno_msg(ex))); return
                item=self._make_item_from_stat(fs_path, arcname, lst, is_symlink_store=True, link_target=target)
                self._add_item(item, pattern_index, internal=internal); return
            else:
                try:
                    fst=os.stat(fs_path)
                except OSError as ex:
                    self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(arcname, errno_msg(ex))); return
                if stat.S_ISDIR(fst.st_mode):
                    self._add_directory(fs_path, arcname, pattern_index, internal=internal, dir_stat=fst)
                    return
                item=self._make_item_from_stat(fs_path, arcname, lst, follow_stat=fst)
                self._add_item(item, pattern_index, internal=internal); return
        if stat.S_ISDIR(lst.st_mode):
            self._add_directory(fs_path, arcname, pattern_index, internal=internal, dir_stat=lst); return
        if stat.S_ISREG(lst.st_mode):
            item=self._make_item_from_stat(fs_path, arcname, lst)
            self._add_item(item, pattern_index, internal=internal); return
        # special file: treat as file (opening may block) - for add/hash 7z would try to read; we add as file with size 0?
        item=self._make_item_from_stat(fs_path, arcname, lst)
        item.size=lst.st_size if hasattr(lst,'st_size') else 0
        self._add_item(item, pattern_index, internal=internal)
    def _add_directory(self, fs_path, arcname, pattern_index, internal=False, dir_stat=None):
        # add dir entry itself unless arcname == '' (root)
        if arcname:
            try:
                lst=dir_stat if dir_stat is not None else os.lstat(fs_path)
                # if symlink to dir following, mode of target
                item=self._make_item_from_stat(fs_path, arcname, lst, follow_stat=lst if not stat.S_ISLNK(lst.st_mode) else dir_stat)
                # ensure dir
                item.is_dir=True
                if item.mode is not None and not stat.S_ISDIR(item.mode):
                    # synthesize dir mode from target
                    item.mode = (dir_stat.st_mode if dir_stat else lst.st_mode)
                self._add_item(item, pattern_index, internal=internal)
            except OSError as ex:
                self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(arcname, errno_msg(ex))); return
        # walk children readdir order
        try:
            entries=list(os.scandir(fs_path))
        except OSError as ex:
            self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(arcname or fs_path, errno_msg(ex))); return
        for child in entries:
            child_fs=os.path.join(fs_path, child.name)
            # skip archive output file
            if self._is_archive_file(child_fs):
                continue
            child_arc=(arcname+'/'+child.name) if arcname else child.name
            if self._excluded(child_arc, child_fs):
                # if dir excluded, skip subtree (scandir check at add will also but we need skip recursion)
                # Determine if exclude pattern exactly matches dir: match_with_dir already true for children too, so skipping here is fine
                # But pattern could match child file only; dir check here uses child_arc for dir itself
                # If child is dir and excluded pattern matches it prefix, skipping
                # We'll let _add_file_path handle files but for dirs we skip by continuing if pattern matches dir itself in sense
                # Simpler: if _excluded uses match_with_dir, children will also be excluded, but dir recursion would waste. continue
                # However a pattern *.log should not prune directories; match for dir name 'sub' vs '*.log' false, so not here
                # Since _excluded(child_arc) true means individual exclusion, skip
                # But for dir traversal with exclude of a file inside, above would be false.
                # ok
                if not stat.S_ISDIR(os.lstat(child_fs).st_mode) if os.path.lexists(child_fs) else False:
                    continue
                # If child is dir but exclude pattern is e.g. '*.log', _excluded false, so not reached
                # If dir matches exclusion, skip
                # Check if child is dir and we are here, skip subtree
                try:
                    if stat.S_ISDIR(os.lstat(child_fs).st_mode):
                        continue
                except Exception:
                    continue
                continue
            self._add_file_path(child_fs, child_arc, pattern_index, internal=True)
    def scan_patterns(self, patterns):
        # patterns: list of strings (already expanded listfiles? Caller expands @)
        if self.opts.si_enabled:
            data=sys.stdin.buffer.read()
            name=self.opts.si_name if self.opts.si_name else 'stdin'
            e=Entry(name, False)
            e.data=data; e.size=len(data); e.scan_size=len(data)
            now_ns=time.time_ns(); e.mtime_ns=now_ns; e.mtime_ft=ns_to_filetime(now_ns)
            e.mode=0o100644; e.win_attr=((0o100644)<<16)|0x8020
            self.items.append(e)
            return self.items
        if not patterns:
            patterns=['*']
        # Include patterns -i add as extra patterns
        extra=[]
        for (recurse, pattern, is_list) in self.opts.include_patterns:
            if is_list:
                extra.extend(read_listfile(pattern, self.opts))
            else:
                extra.append(pattern)
        all_patterns=list(patterns)+extra
        # If include patterns present and original patterns were default? Original 7z: -i can be used instead of file names.
        # Our caller passes patterns explicitly (maybe []), in that case all_patterns will have extras.
        for idx, pat in enumerate(all_patterns):
            self._scan_one_pattern(pat, idx)
        return self.items
    def _scan_one_pattern(self, pat, idx):
        opts=self.opts
        # pattern as given may use backslash as separator? Keep for unix as is except convert \ to / for wildcard matching? Names with backslash rare.
        orig_pat=pat
        # If pattern is empty?
        if pat=='':
            self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(pat, "errno=2 : No such file or directory")); return
        if not has_wildcard(pat, opts):
            # explicit path
            fs_path=pat
            norm=os.path.normpath(fs_path)
            # Check existence (lexists for symlink)
            if not os.path.lexists(fs_path):
                # Display name for warning: as given (pat)
                self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(orig_pat, "errno=2 : No such file or directory")); return
            # arcname
            if norm=='.':
                self._add_directory('.', '', idx, internal=False)
                return
            if os.path.isabs(fs_path) or norm.startswith('../') or norm=='..':
                # arcname basename for file/dir
                lst=os.lstat(fs_path)
                if stat.S_ISDIR(lst.st_mode) or (stat.S_ISLNK(lst.st_mode) and not opts.snl and os.path.isdir(fs_path)):
                    base=os.path.basename(norm.rstrip('/'))
                    self._add_directory(fs_path, base, idx, internal=False)
                else:
                    if opts.spf:
                        arc=fs_path if fs_path.startswith('/') else norm
                        # 7z spf displays leading / in listing; keep as is (strip? observed leading /)
                        arc=arc.replace(os.sep,'/')
                        # Our Entry name normalization may strip later; keep leading / for spf? Entries with leading slash extraction could be dangerous but 7z extracts relative.
                        # For now remove leading /? Real listing shows /tmp/... so keep
                        self._add_file_path(fs_path, arc, idx, internal=False)
                    else:
                        arc=os.path.basename(norm)
                        self._add_file_path(fs_path, arc, idx, internal=False)
                return
            else:
                arc=norm.replace(os.sep,'/')
                self._add_file_path(fs_path, arc, idx, internal=False)
                return
        else:
            # wildcard
            self._scan_wildcard(pat, idx)
            return
    def _scan_wildcard(self, pat, idx):
        opts=self.opts
        # Split pattern into components
        is_abs=os.path.isabs(pat)
        normalized=pat.replace('\\','/')  # for pattern only
        parts=[p for p in normalized.split('/') if p!='']
        # determine prefix dirs (no wildcard)
        prefix_parts=[]
        for part in parts:
            if has_wildcard(part, opts):
                break
            prefix_parts.append(part)
        else:
            prefix_parts=parts  # no wildcard actually
        wildcard_parts=parts[len(prefix_parts):]
        if is_abs:
            base_fs='/'+'/'.join(prefix_parts) if prefix_parts else '/'
            arc_base=''  # arcnames relative to base_fs
        elif prefix_parts and prefix_parts[0]=='..':
            base_fs='/'.join(prefix_parts)
            arc_base=''
        else:
            base_fs='/'.join(prefix_parts) if prefix_parts else '.'
            arc_base='/'.join(prefix_parts) if prefix_parts else ''
        # If prefix is a file? etc.
        # Recursive mode handling
        recur = opts.recurse_mode
        # recurse modes from include spec not handled here (patterns from -i lost recurse). Simplify use global.
        if recur is True or recur=='0':
            # walk base_fs
            if not os.path.isdir(base_fs):
                # if base doesn't exist, warning for pattern?
                if not os.path.lexists(base_fs):
                    self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(pat, "errno=2 : No such file or directory")); return
            # Walk
            def walk(fs_dir, arc_dir):
                try: entries=list(os.scandir(fs_dir))
                except OSError as ex:
                    self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(arc_dir or fs_dir, errno_msg(ex))); return
                for child in entries:
                    child_fs=os.path.join(fs_dir, child.name)
                    if self._is_archive_file(child_fs): continue
                    child_arc=(arc_dir+'/'+child.name) if arc_dir else child.name
                    # full arc candidate for matching: if arc_base is '' but pattern is relative with prefix, pattern matching should be against path relative to cwd?
                    # Build matching path: for relative patterns, matching path = child_arc if arc_base? If base_fs is '.' arc_dir '' child_arc correct.
                    # If base_fs='sub', arc_dir starts 'sub', child_arc = sub/...
                    # That's built by initializing arc_dir=arc_base.
                    # Check if pattern matches child_arc (or for absolute patterns, relative to base)
                    match_target = child_arc if not (is_abs or (prefix_parts and prefix_parts[0]=='..')) else ((child_arc[len(arc_base)+1:] if arc_base and child_arc.startswith(arc_base+'/') else child_arc) if False else os.path.relpath(child_fs, base_fs).replace(os.sep,'/'))
                    # For absolute, 7z wildcard matching: pattern parts after prefix vs relative path; but our wildcard_match_path expects full pattern. Simplify: if is_abs, match against relative and pattern suffix.
                    if is_abs or (prefix_parts and prefix_parts[0]=='..'):
                        pat_for_match='/'.join(parts[len(prefix_parts):]) if parts[len(prefix_parts):] else '*'
                        # pat_for_match may be e.g. *.txt ; matching basename of match_target works
                        matched=wildcard_match_path(pat_for_match, match_target, opts.case_sensitive)
                        # also dir prefix match
                        if not matched:
                            matched=match_with_dir_pattern(pat_for_match, match_target, opts.case_sensitive) and ('*' not in pat_for_match)
                    else:
                        matched=wildcard_match_path(normalized, child_arc, opts.case_sensitive)
                    try: lst=os.lstat(child_fs)
                    except OSError: continue
                    is_dir = stat.S_ISDIR(lst.st_mode) or (stat.S_ISLNK(lst.st_mode) and not opts.snl and os.path.isdir(child_fs))
                    if matched:
                        # add file or directory (directory expansion adds its subcontents, mark internal to avoid duplicates with walking)
                        self._add_file_path(child_fs, child_arc, idx, internal=False)
                        # if directory, _add_file_path already recursed; we should not walk again (duplicates internal dedup will prevent)
                        if is_dir:
                            continue
                    else:
                        if is_dir:
                            walk(child_fs, child_arc)
                # end for
            initial_arc = arc_base if not is_abs else ''
            # For relative pattern with prefix sub, arc_dir should be 'sub'
            walk(base_fs, initial_arc)
            return
        else:
            # non-recursive: pattern matching via component traversal
            # Implement search: starting at base_fs, match wildcard_parts component by component
            # wildcard_parts may include directory components
            if not wildcard_parts:
                self._scan_one_pattern(base_fs, idx); return
            if not os.path.isdir(base_fs):
                if not os.path.lexists(base_fs):
                    self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(pat, "errno=2 : No such file or directory"))
                return
            def search(fs_dir, arc_dir, comp_index):
                if comp_index>=len(wildcard_parts):
                    return
                comp=wildcard_parts[comp_index]
                try: entries=list(os.scandir(fs_dir))
                except OSError as ex:
                    self.warnings.append(ScanWarning(arc_dir or fs_dir, errno_msg(ex))); return
                for child in entries:
                    if self._is_archive_file(os.path.join(fs_dir, child.name)): continue
                    if not wildcard_match_component(comp, child.name, opts.case_sensitive):
                        continue
                    child_fs=os.path.join(fs_dir, child.name)
                    child_arc=(arc_dir+'/'+child.name) if arc_dir else child.name
                    if comp_index==len(wildcard_parts)-1:
                        self._add_file_path(child_fs, child_arc, idx, internal=False)
                    else:
                        # must be dir to continue
                        if os.path.isdir(child_fs):
                            search(child_fs, child_arc, comp_index+1)
            search(base_fs, arc_base if not is_abs else '', 0)
            return

def read_listfile(path, opts):
    # Listfile charset default UTF-8? -scs
    try:
        # Detect UTF-16 BOM
        raw=open(path,'rb').read()
        if raw.startswith(b'\xff\xfe'):
            text=raw.decode('utf-16le')
        elif raw.startswith(b'\xfe\xff'):
            text=raw.decode('utf-16be')

def mode_string(mode, is_dir=False):
    if mode is None:
        # synthesize
        if is_dir: return "drwxr-xr-x"
        return "-rw-r--r--"
    ft = stat.S_IFMT(mode)
    if stat.S_ISDIR(mode): c='d'
    elif stat.S_ISLNK(mode): c='l'
    elif stat.S_ISREG(mode): c='-'
    elif stat.S_ISFIFO(mode): c='p'
    elif stat.S_ISSOCK(mode): c='s'
    elif stat.S_ISCHR(mode): c='c'
    elif stat.S_ISBLK(mode): c='b'
    else: c='?'
    chars=[c]
    for who in [(0o400,0o200,0o100, stat.S_ISUID, 's'), (0o040,0o020,0o010, stat.S_ISGID, 's'), (0o004,0o002,0o001, stat.S_ISVTX, 't')]:
        r,w,x,special,schar = who
        chars.append('r' if mode&r else '-')
        chars.append('w' if mode&w else '-')
        if mode & special:
            chars.append(schar if mode&x else schar.upper())
        else:
            chars.append('x' if mode&x else '-')
    return ''.join(chars)

# Wildcard matching
def has_wildcard(s, opts=None):
    if opts is not None and opts.spd:
        return False
    return '*' in s or '?' in s

def wildcard_match_component(pattern, name, case_sensitive=True):
    if not case_sensitive:
        pattern=pattern.lower(); name=name.lower()
    # convert to regex
    regex='^'
    for ch in pattern:
        if ch=='*': regex+='.*'
        elif ch=='?': regex+='.'
        else: regex+=re.escape(ch)
    regex+='$'
    return re.match(regex, name, re.DOTALL) is not None

def wildcard_match_path(pattern, path, case_sensitive=True):
    # pattern and path use '/'
    if '/' not in pattern:
        name=path.split('/')[-1]
        return wildcard_match_component(pattern, name, case_sensitive)
    pparts=pattern.split('/'); nparts=path.split('/')
    if len(pparts)!=len(nparts):
        return False
    return all(wildcard_match_component(pp,nn,case_sensitive) for pp,nn in zip(pparts,nparts))

def match_with_dir_pattern(pattern, path, case_sensitive=True):
    # Pattern matching used for archive selection/deletion/extraction:
    # - exact/wildcard full match
    # - if pattern matches a directory name (prefix), all under it match (for non-wildcard dir pattern or wildcard matching dir)
    # returns (selected, is_dir_match?) Caller handles
    if wildcard_match_path(pattern, path, case_sensitive):
        return True
    # pattern without wildcard and path under pattern/
    if '*' not in pattern and '?' not in pattern:
        pat=pattern.rstrip('/')
        if path==pat or path.startswith(pat+'/'):
            return True
    # wildcard pattern could match a leading directory: e.g. pattern 'adir' checked above; pattern '*'? Already full match only component wise; '*' vs 'adir/x.txt' len mismatch so not.
    # If pattern matches a prefix directory of path (for patterns like 'a*' matching dir)
    parts=path.split('/'); pparts=pattern.split('/')
    if len(pparts)<len(parts):
        prefix='/'.join(parts[:len(pparts)])
        if wildcard_match_path(pattern, prefix, case_sensitive):
            return True
    return False

    try:
        # Detect UTF-16 BOM
        raw=open(path,'rb').read()
        if raw.startswith(b'\xff\xfe'):

        elif raw.startswith(b'\xfe\xff'):
            text=raw.decode('utf-16be')
        elif raw.startswith(b'\xef\xbb\xbf'):

            if opts.charset_list and opts.charset_list.lower()=='utf-16le':
                text=raw.decode('utf-16le')
            elif opts.charset_list and opts.charset_list.lower()=='utf-16be':
                text=raw.decode('utf-16be')
            else:
                text=raw.decode('utf-8', errors='surrogateescape')
        lines=[]
        for line in text.splitlines():
            if line.startswith('\ufeff'): line=line[1:]

# ---------- ZIP format ----------
def dos_datetime(dt):
    if dt is None: return (0,0)
    # dt is datetime local
    if dt.year<1980: dt=dt.replace(year=1980,month=1,day=1,hour=0,minute=0,second=0)
    dostime=(dt.hour<<11)|(dt.minute<<5)|(dt.second//2)
    dosdate=((dt.year-1980)<<9)|(dt.month<<5)|dt.day
    return (dostime,dosdate)
def datetime_from_dos(dostime,dosdate, ft=None):
    if ft is not None and ft!=0:
        return ft_to_datetime(ft)
    sec=(dostime & 0x1F)*2; minute=(dostime>>5)&0x3F; hour=(dostime>>11)&0x1F
    day=dosdate & 0x1F; month=(dosdate>>5)&0x0F; year=((dosdate>>9)&0x7F)+1980
    try: return datetime(year,month or 1,day or 1,hour,minute,sec)
    except Exception: return None
def parse_extra_fields(extra):
    fields=[]
    i=0
    while i+4<=len(extra):
        hid, sz=struct.unpack_from('<HH', extra, i); i+=4
        fields.append((hid, extra[i:i+sz])); i+=sz
    return fields
def parse_ntfs_extra(extra):
    times={}
    for hid,data in parse_extra_fields(extra):
        if hid==0x000A:
            # reserved 4, then tags
            j=4
            while j+4<=len(data):
                tag, sz=struct.unpack_from('<HH', data, j); j+=4
                val=data[j:j+sz]; j+=sz
                if tag==0x0001 and len(val)>=24:
                    m,c,a=struct.unpack_from('<QQQ', val,0)
                    if m: times['m']=m
                    if c: times['c']=c
                    if a: times['a']=a
                elif tag==0x0001 and len(val)>=8:
                    times['m']=struct.unpack_from('<Q',val,0)[0]

        if hid==0x5455: # extended timestamp
            times['ut']=data

def zip_method_name(code, encrypted_kind=None):
    names={0:'Store',8:'Deflate',9:'Deflate64',12:'BZip2',14:'LZMA',93:'???',95:'XZ',98:'PPMD'}
    base=names.get(code, f"Method{code}")
    if encrypted_kind=='aes':

def load_zip_entry_data(arch, entry, opts, password):
    if not getattr(entry,'_zip_pending',False):

def derive_single_name(path, fmt):

        if low.endswith('.gzip'): return base[:-5]
        if low.endswith('.gz'): return base[:-3]
        return base
    if fmt=='bzip2':
        if low.endswith('.bzip2'): return base[:-6]
        if low.endswith('.bz2'): return base[:-4]
        if low.endswith('.tbz2'): return base[:-5]+'.tar'
        if low.endswith('.tbz'): return base[:-4]+'.tar'

    if fmt=='xz':
        if low.endswith('.xz'): return base[:-3]
        if low.endswith('.txz'): return base[:-4]+'.tar'
        return base
    if fmt=='lzma':
        if low.endswith('.lzma'): return base[:-5]
        if low.endswith('.lzma86'): return base[:-7]
        return base
    return base

    method=HASH_EXT_METHODS.get(ext)
    text=data.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape')
    entries=[]
    # If first lines look like hash lines
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if not line.strip(): continue
        if line.lstrip().startswith('#'): continue
        m=re.match(r'^([0-9a-fA-F]+)\s+\*?(.*)$', line)
        if not m: continue
        hexval, name=m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()

        if not method:

    bits_map={'crc32':32,'crc64':64,'xxh64':64,'md5':128,'sha1':160,'sha256':256,'sha512':512,'sha384':384,'sha224':224}
    bits=bits_map.get(method or 'sha256', digest_bytes*8)
    arch.props['Characteristics']=f"{bits}-bit filename_method:{method or 'sha256'}"
    return arch

# Wrap original archive_info_lines

                # Need check raw_positionals vs actual? parse_args stored positionals after first as raw_positionals. But when switches precede command, that's still ok.
                # However if command came from positionals, raw_positionals is positionals[1:] already.
                # Determine archive name: we stored raw_positionals as after-command; that includes archive as first? Wait parse_args: positionals[0] is command, raw = positionals[1:] includes archive name as first element.
                # So archive_name should be raw[0], file_names raw[1:]
                if len(opts.raw_positionals)>=0:
                    pass
            if not opts.raw_positionals and not opts.include_archives:
                out(get_banner()+"\n")
                print_cmdline_error("Cannot find archive name")
                return 7
            if opts.raw_positionals:
                opts.archive_name=opts.raw_positionals[0]
                opts.file_names=opts.raw_positionals[1:]
                # For subsequent code, raw_positionals should represent file names only
                opts.raw_positionals=opts.file_names
            else:
                opts.archive_name=None
    else:
        # h: raw_positionals are files (already after command)
        opts.file_names=opts.raw_positionals
    # print banner for all successful parse commands (to output stream)
    # For -so, OUT_MODE=0 so nothing printed
    out(get_banner()+"\n")
    exit_code=0
    try:
        if cmd=='i':
            exit_code=do_info(opts)
        elif cmd=='b':
            exit_code=do_benchmark(opts)
        elif cmd=='h':
            exit_code=do_hash(opts)
        elif cmd=='l':
            exit_code=do_list(opts)
        elif cmd in ('t','e','x'):
            exit_code=do_test_extract(opts, is_extract=(cmd in ('e','x')))
        elif cmd in ('a','u'):
            exit_code=do_add_update(opts, cmd)
        elif cmd=='d':
            exit_code=do_delete(opts)
        elif cmd=='rn':
            exit_code=do_rename(opts)
        else:
            exit_code=0
    except UserBreak:
        err_out("\n\nBreak signaled\n"); exit_code=255
    except BrokenPipeError:
        try: sys.stdout.close()
        except Exception: pass
        exit_code=0
    except CmdLineError as e:
        print_cmdline_error(e.detail); exit_code=7
    except FatalError as fe:
        if fe.kind=='system': print_system_error(fe.msg)
        else: print_error_head(fe.msg)
        exit_code=2
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        err_out("\n\nBreak signaled\n"); exit_code=255
    if opts.bt and exit_code==0:
        global_elapsed=time.time()-start_global
        # similar format: blank line?
        out("\n")
        out(f"Kernel  Time =     0.000 =    0%\n")
        out(f"User    Time =     {time.process_time():.3f} =    0%\n")
        # Approx percentages
        out(f"Process Time =     {time.process_time():.3f} =    0%\n")
        out(f"Global  Time =     {global_elapsed:.3f} =  100%\n")
    return exit_code

if __name__=='__main__':
    try:
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
    except BrokenPipeError:
        sys.exit(0)

import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('/tmp/harness.py'); t=p.read_text()
t=t.replace("def norm(s):\n    # mask archive sizes etc? keep for viewing but mark lines\n    return s", "def norm(s):\n    import re\n    s=re.sub(r'(Archive size: ).*',r'\\1<X>',s)\n    s=re.sub(r'(Physical Size = ).*',r'\\1<X>',s)\n    s=re.sub(r'(Headers Size = ).*',r'\\1<X>',s)\n    return s")
# apply norm in compare when comparing/reporting stdout
t=t.replace("if a[1]!=b[1] or a[2]!=b[2] or a[3]!=b[3]:", "a=(a[0],a[1],norm(a[2]),a[3]); b=(b[0],b[1],norm(b[2]),b[3])\n        if a[1]!=b[1] or a[2]!=b[2] or a[3]!=b[3]:")
# snapshot: ignore archive files hash/size
t=t.replace("            items.append(f\"{rel} sz={sz} sha={h}\")", "            items.append(f\"{rel} sz={sz} sha={h}\" if not rel.endswith(('.7z','.zip','.tar','.gz','.xz','.bz2')) else f\"{rel} archive\")")
p.write_text(t)
PY
# patch tar recordsize and files_read and test summary blank
python3 - << 'PY'
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('/workspace/sevenzip.py'); t=p.read_text()
t=t.replace("tf=tarfile.open(fileobj=out, mode='w', format=tarfile.GNU_FORMAT)", "tf=tarfile.open(fileobj=out, mode='w', format=tarfile.GNU_FORMAT, bufsize=512)")
# tarfile bufsize may not be recordsize parameter in open; tarfile.open has bufsize which sets recordsize? In python, TarFile.bufsize is record size used for padding. Use that.
# add/ update files_read for tar: modify counting after loops: simplest after files_read loop set if typ tar
t=t.replace("    add_items=read_items\n    # Categories counts", "    add_items=read_items\n    if typ=='tar':\n        files_read=len(add_items)\n    # Categories counts")
# test/extract summary blank fix
t=t.replace("""            if len(selected)==0:
                out("\\n\\nNo files to process\\n")
            else:
                out("\\n")
            out("Everything is Ok\\n")""",
"""            if len(selected)==0:
                out("\\nNo files to process\\n")
            out("Everything is Ok\\n")""")
p.write_text(t)
print('patched')
PY
python3 /tmp/harness.py > /tmp/harness_out.txt 2>&1; grep -E "SCENARIO|RESULT|STEP " /tmp/harness_out.txt

import hashlib
files=[(b'hello.txt',b'hello world\n'),(b'second.txt',b'second file content\n')]
ds=[hashlib.sha256(d).digest() for _,d in files]
def toi(b): return int.from_bytes(b,'big')
def tol(b): return int.from_bytes(b,'little')
s=(toi(ds[0])+toi(ds[1]))%(1<<256)
print('sum big', s.to_bytes(32,'big').hex())
s=(tol(ds[0])+tol(ds[1]))%(1<<256)
print('sum little word? ', s.to_bytes(32,'little').hex())
# xor
print('xor', bytes(a^b for a,b in zip(ds[0],ds[1])).hex())
# filenames combined: maybe sum of hash(name+data) ?
nds=[hashlib.sha256(n.decode().encode('utf-16le')+d).digest() for n,d in [(b'hello.txt',files[0][1]),(b'second.txt',files[1][1])]]
s=(toi(nds[0])+toi(nds[1]))%(1<<256)
print('names sum big', s.to_bytes(32,'big').hex())
# maybe hash(name utf16 + data) per file combined sum of digests of (name+data)
# other per file: hash of name alone + data etc

    Reimplement 7-Zip (7za) command line archiver from observed behavior
    
    Pure-Python implementation of the 7za 26.00 CLI, written from black-box
    probing of the reference binary. Supports:
    - Commands: a, u, d, rn, e, x, l, t, h, i, b
    - Formats (read/write): 7z, zip (incl. ZipCrypto and WinZip AES),
      tar, gzip, bzip2, xz, lzma and the Hash checksum format
    - 7z codec handling (LZMA/LZMA2/Copy/Deflate/BZip2/BCJ/Delta chains),
      solid and non-solid archives, encoded and AES-encrypted headers,
      Zip64, multi-volume (split) archives, symlink handling,
      include/exclude/listfile patterns, wildcards and recursion modes,
      stdin/stdout streaming, overwrite prompts and modes
    
    compile.sh copies the single-file Python implementation to ./executable.
